fields.Participants: Procurement Analyst, Procurement Mgr, VP Supply Chain

Automation Opportunity: - Report auto-generated from the W2458 calc output (no manual assembly); action-prompt tags auto-derived from the mover/threshold rules
Controls: - CTL-48: rebate-dispute frequency surfaced as a scorecard input — visible in the monthly report; operational: Procurement Manager sign-off on the published report
Pain Points / Risks: - **Report-fatigue risk**: a 1,000-vendor report is noise unless the bottom-20 and biggest-movers are foregrounded; mitigated by the "review required by" tagging that turns the report into a worklist, not a reference document

- **Lagging-signal risk**: a monthly report surfaces a problem 30 days after the transactions that caused it; mitigated by the W2460 new-vendor weekly cadence and the exception-driven W2455 daily monitoring for high-volume vendors
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the monthly report is a curated view over the W2458 supplier-performance fact table; the same dashboard Buyers self-service during the month
- Supplier-performance module (W2458) — source of the composite scores and per-dimension drill-downs
- Distribution/notification (links to VS-63 store-comms pattern, applied HQ-side) — report delivered to each Category Manager's queue with the action-prompt tags
Time Estimate: ~4–6 hours/month Procurement Analyst (curation + annotation + distribution) = **~48–72 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Generates the monthly report package from the W2458 scorecard output: top-20 performers, bottom-20 performers, biggest movers (±15 points month-over-month), new additions (first-scored vendors from W2460), KPI trend lines per dimension; distributes to Category Managers and Buyers with action-prompt annotations (each bottom-20 / biggest-mover entry carries a "review required by" tag)

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Procurement Mgr, Vendor, VP Supply Chain

Automation Opportunity: - Scorecard-vs-target view auto-prepared for each review (opens with last quarter's agreed targets and current actuals); joint-action-plan template auto-populated from the discussion
Controls: - CTL-177 (ensure vendor scorecard data quality & performance action.)
- Operational: VP Supply Chain reviews any strategic-vendor target miss before it escalates to W2465 (prevents a single Category Manager from unilaterally PIP-ing a strategic relationship)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Soft-target risk**: 90-day targets agreed in the room are vague ("improve delivery") and unmeasurable at the next review; mitigated by the target being recorded as a specific KPI threshold (e.g., "OTD 92%→95% by Q-end") in the system, not just meeting notes

- **Asymmetry risk**: the vendor sees BuildRight's scorecard but BuildRight doesn't see the vendor's view of BuildRight as a customer (payment behavior, forecast accuracy); mitigated by an annual two-way scorecard exchange for the top 20 strategic vendors
System Touchpoints: - Supplier-performance module (W2458) — the scorecard artifact presented in the review, and where the 90-day targets are recorded
- CRM / supplier-relationship artifact (links to VS-03 / W36 vendor-master, VS-100 legal for joint-development agreements) — the joint action plan and vendor roadmap stored against the vendor record
- Benchmark dataset (W2461) — the market-percentile framing that makes "improvement" concrete
Time Estimate: ~1.5 hours/vendor/quarter + ~30 min/target-recording × 50 strategic vendors ≈ 75–125 hours ≈ **~75–125 hours/quarter** distributed across ~5 Category Managers (≈ 15–25 hours each/quarter, ~1.5–2 hours/week — core vendor-management duty).

steps.activity: Category Manager conducts a structured review with the strategic vendor: presents the W2458 scorecard with the W2461 benchmark percentile, discusses strengths and improvement areas, agrees 90-day improvement targets documented in a joint action plan; vendor presents their roadmap (new products, capacity, sustainability initiatives)

Category Manager records the agreed targets in the supplier-performance module so the next quarter's review opens with a scorecard-vs-target view; escalates any target miss to the W2465 PIP workflow if a threshold breach accompanies it

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Procurement Mgr, Category Mgrs, CFO

Automation Opportunity: - Draft tier assignment auto-generated from the annual scorecard rollup + the prior-year tier (VP Supply Chain reviews the diff, not the full list); tier-change communications auto-drafted
Controls: - CTL-06 (vendor-master integrity — the tier tag must be current, since it drives payment terms and allocation); operational: CFO approval on tier changes affecting Strategic/Platinum vendors (commercial-materiality control)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tier-inertia risk**: vendors stay in a tier by precedent rather than current performance (a formerly-strategic vendor now mid-pack keeps Platinum); mitigated by the annual forced re-classification against current scorecard, with any tier-change documented and communicated

- **Concentration risk**: 45% of COGS in the top 20 vendors means a single tier-down or delisting has outsized supply impact; mitigated by the dual-source requirement for Strategic-tier items (links to VS-02 supply planning) flagged at classification
System Touchpoints: - Supplier-performance module (W2458) — the annual scorecard rollup (12-month composite + per-dimension averages) is the classification input
- Vendor-master (links to VS-29 / W287) — the tier tag is written to the vendor master, where it drives PO-allocation logic, payment-term selection, and co-op-budget eligibility
- Co-op/rebate accrual (links to VS-39 / W27) — tier drives the rebate-tier rate in the rebate agreement master
Time Estimate: ~5–10 days/year VP Supply Chain classification + ~1–2 days CFO/CEO commercial-terms sign-off = **~50–100 hours/year**.

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain classifies vendors into five tiers from the annual scorecard rollup: (a) Strategic/Platinum — top 20 vendors (~45% of COGS), (b) Preferred/Gold — next 50, (c) Approved/Silver — standard, (d) Probation/Bronze — underperforming, (e) Watch/At-Risk — potential for delisting per W2466

Tier determines commercial treatment: PO allocation priority, payment terms, co-op marketing budget (links to VS-39 rebates), strategic-collaboration level (joint business planning), vendor-development investment (links to VS-67.3)

fields.Participants: Procurement Mgr, Category Mgr, Vendor, VP Supply Chain

Automation Opportunity: - PIP auto-triggered when a vendor breaches threshold for N consecutive months (not waiting for manual detection); graduation/escalation auto-suggested from the scorecard-vs-target state at day 90
Controls: - CTL-48: rebate-dispute pattern is one PIP trigger — commercial and performance signals converge here; operational: PIP-outcome follow-through sampled in the W2459 quarterly audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **PIP-as-theatre risk**: the plan is issued but the consequence is never enforced, training vendors that underperformance has no cost; mitigated by the documented escalation path (PIP miss → W2466) and the quarterly W2459 audit checking PIP-outcome follow-through

- **Moving-goalpost risk**: the PIP targets are redefined mid-window to let the vendor pass; mitigated by the targets being locked in the system at PIP issuance and change-controlled (VP Supply Chain approval to modify)
System Touchpoints: - Supplier-performance module (W2458) — the PIP is tracked as a workflow state on the vendor record; the monthly check-in reads the live scorecard against the PIP targets
- Vendor-master (links to VS-29 / W287) — "PIP active" flag blocks new Strategic-tier benefits until graduation
- Document control (links to VS-88) — the formal PIP letter and the monthly check-in notes are versioned artifacts (audit trail)
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/PIP issuance + ~3 hours/PIP monitoring (1 hour × 3 monthly check-ins) × ~25 PIPs/year = **~140–160 hours/year** Procurement Manager.

steps.activity: Procurement Manager issues a formal PIP to the underperforming vendor: cites the specific KPIs below threshold (from W2458), the required improvement levels, the 90-day timeline, and the consequences if not met (volume reduction or escalation to W2466 delisting); documents in the vendor record

Monthly check-ins during the PIP window: vendor reports corrective actions taken, Procurement validates improvement against the W2458 monthly scorecard; if targets met → graduate from PIP with the improved baseline locked; if not → escalate to the W2466 delisting review

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Mgr, Procurement, Finance, Legal

Automation Opportunity: - Delisting-checklist workflow (legal notice → portal revocation → master status → AP block) sequenced with sign-offs; the alternative-vendor capacity check drawn from VS-02 supply planning
Controls: - CTL-06: vendor-master status — the "do not pay" block is the key fraud-prevention control on a delisted vendor; CTL-42 (bank-account-change guard — prevents a delisted vendor's last-payment reroute); operational: CFO + Legal sign-off on every delisting
Pain Points / Risks: - **Supply-gap risk**: delisting before the alternative vendor can absorb volume causes stockouts on the affected items; mitigated by the prerequisite "alternative qualified + volume-confirmed" gate in step 1, enforced via the dual-source flag from W2464

- **Retaliation/transition-disruption risk**: a delisted vendor delays final shipments, withholds repair parts, or disputes the final settlement; mitigated by the contractual termination-notice check in step 2 and Finance escrowing the final payment pending clean handover
System Touchpoints: - Vendor-master (links to VS-29 / W287, CTL-06) — the "delisted" status blocks new POs and triggers the AP-do-not-pay check; stale-delisted-vendor cleanup links to CTL-51
- Supplier portal (links to VS-28 / W593) — access revoked; open ASN/invoice workflow closed out
- Contract repository (links to VS-100 / W230 legal contract review) — termination-notice period and any early-termination penalty verified before the ramp-down starts
Time Estimate: ~4 days/delisting for step 1 (VP Supply Chain + Category Manager) + ~45-day ramp-down in step 2 (mostly monitoring, ~10–15 hours of active work spread across Finance/Procurement/Legal) × ~7 delistings/year = **~200–280 hours/year** total across functions.

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain initiates the delisting: documents the performance history, the W2465 PIP results, the quantified business impact (stockouts, quality costs, expedite fees); confirms an alternative vendor is qualified and can absorb the volume (links to VS-02 supply planning); presents the recommendation to the Category Manager and CFO

Category Manager approves the alternative sourcing; Procurement transitions the volume over a defined ramp-down; Finance settles final payments and any open rebates/consignment (links to VS-39, VS-45); Legal reviews contractual obligations and termination notice; vendor-portal access revoked (links to VS-28/W593) and the vendor-master set to "inactive — do not pay" (CTL-06)

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Procurement Mgr, Category Mgrs, CEO

Automation Opportunity: - Award-eligibility auto-shortlisted from the annual scorecard (VP Supply Chain curates the shortlist, doesn't assemble it); recipient communications and benefit-activation auto-drafted
Controls: - CTL-431 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Performance Review & Rating (PA-67.2).)
- Operational: CEO sign-off on Vendor of the Year (reputational-materiality control); award selection criteria documented and retained (audit trail for any "why not us" vendor query)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Perception-of-favoritism risk**: an award without a visible scorecard basis looks like cronyism to non-recipients; mitigated by awards tracing to the W2458 objective scorecard and the selection criteria published to the vendor base

- **Award-without-reward risk**: a plaque with no commercial benefit becomes meaningless; mitigated by the tangible benefits in step 2 (allocation, terms, co-marketing) that make the award materially valuable
System Touchpoints: - Supplier-performance module (W2458) + annual classification (W2464) — the objective basis for award selection (awards are not subjective; they trace to the scorecard)
- Vendor-master / co-marketing budget (links to VS-39 / VS-14 marketing) — award-tier benefits recorded against the vendor record and the marketing co-op budget
- Event logistics (links to VS-139 event-marketing pattern, applied supplier-side) — summit coordination
Time Estimate: ~4 days/year VP Supply Chain selection + event + 1 day benefit-activation = **~40 hours/year**, plus event logistics absorbed into VS-139.

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain identifies award recipients from the annual W2464 tier classification and W2458 scorecard: Vendor of the Year (highest composite), Quality Excellence (best quality dimension), Delivery Reliability (best OTD/fill), Innovation Partner (best innovation dimension / new-SKU contribution), Sustainability Champion (best ESG/sustainable-sourcing evidence per VS-25/VS-131); coordinates a recognition event (annual supplier summit or virtual)

Awards carry commercial weight: increased PO allocation priority, preferred payment terms, co-marketing opportunities, and a strategic-partnership discussion (joint business planning); reinforces the performance culture and signals to the vendor base what excellence looks like

fields.Participants: IT Business Analyst, Procurement Mgr, VP Supply Chain

Automation Opportunity: - Usage telemetry on the dashboards (which views, which users, how often) to prioritize enhancements by actual adoption rather than anecdote
Controls: - CTL-51: master-data/stale-data checks — applies to the scorecard fact table the enhancements touch; operational: enhancements released via W132 change management with Procurement Manager UAT sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Enhancement-without-adoption risk**: IT ships a new dashboard nobody uses because Buyers weren't consulted on the design; mitigated by the user-feedback input in step 1 and a pilot with 2–3 Category Managers before full release

- **Calc-drift risk**: an enhancement to the calc engine silently changes historical scores (a retroactive re-tier); mitigated by versioned calc logic and a "recompute historical?" decision gate requiring VP Supply Chain approval
System Touchpoints: - Supplier-performance module (W2458) and the W2455 data pipeline — the systems under enhancement
- Analytics/BI platform (links to VS-27 / W113) — the dashboard layer; enhancements follow the BI governance standard
- IT change management (links to VS-27 / W132 IT change management) — enhancements released through the standard change pipeline, not ad-hoc
Time Estimate: ~5–10 days/quarter IT Business Analyst = **~80–160 hours/year**, absorbed into the IT procurement-systems roadmap.

steps.activity: IT reviews the scorecard system end-to-end: reporting capabilities, data-visualization usability, integration completeness (are all W2455 source feeds flowing?), user feedback from Buyers/Category Managers; implements prioritized enhancements — new KPIs (e.g., sustainability dimension), better dashboards (mobile access for Buyers on the floor), faster calc-cycle latency

fields.Frequency: Quarterly; 5 functions (Procurement, Quality, Finance, Store Ops, Merchandising)
fields.Participants: Procurement Mgr, Quality Mgr, Finance Mgr, VP Store Operations, Category Mgrs

Automation Opportunity: - Each function's extract auto-pulled from its source module (no manual submission); the integration rollup auto-computed with the Procurement Manager reviewing exceptions only
Controls: - CTL-24: receiving-fraud detection — Store Ops feedback that surfaces anomalous receiving patterns feeds back into CTL-24's monitoring; operational: cross-functional inputs retained as audit trail for any subsequent W2465 PIP or W2466 delisting decision
Pain Points / Risks: - **Anecdote-over-data risk**: Store Ops submits "deliveries are always late lately" without the underlying receipt data; mitigated by the structured extract requirement (each function submits its module's data, not just impressions)

- **Dominant-function risk**: Finance's invoice-dispute view dominates because it's the most quantified, drowning out Quality's softer signals; mitigated by the pre-agreed dimension weights and Procurement Manager judgment in the integration
System Touchpoints: - Source modules per function: Quality (VS-31), Finance/AP (VS-15/W7), Store Ops receiving (VS-04/W3), Merchandising (VS-01) — each provides a structured extract; the integration is Procurement's rollup
- Supplier-performance module (W2458) — the destination; cross-functional signals feed the qualitative dimension alongside the W2457 internal survey
- Collaboration tooling (cross-functional workspace or the procurement module's feedback sub-form) — structured capture rather than email
Time Estimate: ~5 hours/quarter Procurement Manager integration + ~1 hour/quarter × 4 other functions (extract prep) = ~9 hours/quarter ≈ **~36–40 hours/year** total across functions.

steps.activity: Procurement collects structured cross-functional feedback per strategic vendor: Quality (inspection trends from W110/W681), Finance (invoice-dispute frequency and payment-terms compliance from W7/W100), Store Ops (delivery-quality / receiving experience from W3/W681), Merchandising (product quality and trend-responsiveness from VS-01/VS-14); integrates the weighted signals into the qualitative dimension of the W2458 composite
